name: Slow Cooker Dr Pepper Pulled Pork Bowls
intro_html: The soda cooks off and leaves behind a sweet, caramel-like depth that makes this pulled pork taste like a backyard cookout. Piled over potatoes, each bowl carries 56 grams of protein for around $2.28 (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings from one pot is barbecue money well spent.
ingredients_display: BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free) (Sweet Baby Ray's): 1 bottle (360 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free), 1 bottle: ~$2.21. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper, garlic powder): ~$0.12. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $23.86 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.70 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $26.71 across 14 servings, roughly $1.91 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $5.15 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $31.86. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $2.28 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: Use zero-sugar soda to get the caramelized flavor without the extra sugar and calories. It works just as well as the regular stuff.
A sugar-free BBQ sauce keeps the carbs down while still giving you that tangy, smoky finish.
Potatoes are your cheapest base by far. A 9 lb bag stretches this whole batch and then some for very little money.
make_it: Rub the pork loin all over with the salt, black pepper, and garlic powder, then set it in the slow cooker and scatter the sliced onion around it.
Pour the zero-sugar soda over the pork until it is about halfway up the sides.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork shreds easily.
Drain off most of the liquid, then shred the pork right in the pot.
Stir in the BBQ sauce and let it warm through for a few minutes.
Serve over cooked potatoes and divide into containers.
portion_html: Each serving lands near 557 calories with 56 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from Spend With Pennies, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
